nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-01.title: Pairs of vertices minus sides
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-01.body:
There are $\binom{12}2=66$ segments joining two vertices; $12$ of them are sides, so $66-12=54$ are diagonals.

**Answer: 54**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-01.title: Formula
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-01.body:
Each vertex connects to $12-3=9$ others by diagonals; each diagonal is counted twice: $\frac{12\cdot9}{2}=54$.

**Answer: 54**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-02.title: Track the acid
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-02.body:
The solution contains $0.3\cdot12=3.6$ ounces of acid. Adding $x$ ounces of acid: $\frac{3.6+x}{12+x}=0.4$, so $3.6+x=4.8+0.4x$, $0.6x=1.2$, $x=2$.

**Answer: 2 ounces**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-02.title: Track the water
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-02.body:
The water, $8.4$ ounces, does not change. In the final solution it is $60\%$, so the total is $\frac{8.4}{0.6}=14$ ounces: add $2$ ounces of acid.

**Answer: 2 ounces**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-03.title: Reverse the polynomial
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-03.body:
The reciprocals of the roots are the roots of $-10x^2-7x+2=0$ (coefficients reversed), whose root sum is $-\frac{-7}{-10}=-\frac7{10}$.

**Answer: $-\frac7{10}$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-04.title: Subtract two segments
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-04.body:
Each chord is at distance $4=\frac12\cdot8$ from the center, so it subtends a central angle of $120^\circ$. The segment cut off beyond it has area
$$\tfrac13\cdot64\pi-\tfrac12\cdot8^2\sin120^\circ=\tfrac{64\pi}3-16\sqrt3.$$
The region between the chords is the circle minus two such segments:
$$64\pi-2\left(\tfrac{64\pi}3-16\sqrt3\right)=\tfrac{64\pi}3+32\sqrt3.$$

**Answer: $32\sqrt3+\frac{64\pi}{3}$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-04.title: Add the pieces directly
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-04.body:
Take the chords on the lines $y=4$ and $y=-4$. Their endpoints are at angles $30^\circ, 150^\circ$ and $210^\circ, 330^\circ$ on the circle. The region between the chords splits into
- two triangles joining the center to each chord, each with two sides $8$ and included angle $120^\circ$: area $2\cdot\frac12\cdot64\sin120^\circ=32\sqrt3$;
- two $60^\circ$ sectors (from $330^\circ$ to $30^\circ$ and from $150^\circ$ to $210^\circ$): area $2\cdot\frac{64\pi}{6}=\frac{64\pi}{3}$.

Total $32\sqrt3+\frac{64\pi}3$.

**Answer: $32\sqrt3+\frac{64\pi}{3}$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-07.title: Alternating digit sum
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-07.body:
A number is divisible by $11$ when its alternating digit sum is. From the right: $7-x+8-6+9-2=16-x$. For a digit $x$, $16-x$ is a multiple of $11$ only when $x=5$. Check: $296857=11\cdot26987$.

**Answer: 5**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-08.title: Area = rs
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-08.body:
The hypotenuse is $5$, the area is $6$ and the semiperimeter is $6$. From $\text{Area}=rs$, $r=\frac66=1$.

**Answer: 1**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-10.title: Geometric series
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-10.body:
Bill wins on his 1st, 2nd, 3rd, … turn with probabilities $\frac12$, $\frac12\cdot\frac14$, $\frac12\cdot\frac1{16}$, … The sum is $\frac{1/2}{1-1/4}=\frac23$.

**Answer: $\frac23$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-10.title: Recursion
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-10.body:
Let $p$ be the probability that the person about to flip wins. Either they flip a head now ($\frac12$), or they flip a tail and then they are in the other player's position: $p=\frac12+\frac12(1-p)$, so $p=\frac23$.

**Answer: $\frac23$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-12.title: Similar triangles (golden triangle)
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-12.body:
Let the triangle be $ABC$ with $AB=AC=2$, $\angle A=36^\circ$, base $BC=x$; the base angles are $72^\circ$. Bisect $\angle B$, meeting $AC$ at $D$. Then $\angle DBC=36^\circ$ and $\angle BDC=72^\circ$, so $BD=BC=x$, and $\angle ABD=36^\circ=\angle A$ gives $AD=BD=x$. Triangle $BCD$ is similar to $ABC$, so $\frac{CD}{BC}=\frac{BC}{AB}$: $\frac{2-x}{x}=\frac x2$. Then $x^2+2x-4=0$ and $x=-1+\sqrt5$.

**Answer: $\sqrt5-1$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-12.title: Trigonometry
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-12.body:
The altitude from the vertex bisects the base and the $36^\circ$ angle, so the base is $2\cdot2\sin18^\circ=4\cdot\frac{\sqrt5-1}4=\sqrt5-1$.

**Answer: $\sqrt5-1$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-13.title: List them
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-13.body:
Units digit $7$ (tens digit not $7$): $17, 37, 47, 67, 97$ are prime ($27, 57, 87$ are not). Tens digit $7$ (units digit not $7$): $71, 73, 79$. Total $8$.

**Answer: 8**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-14.title: Mean proportionals
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-14.body:
A leg is the mean proportional between the hypotenuse and its adjacent segment: $AC^2=AD\cdot AB$, so $36=AD(AD+5)$, giving $AD=4$ and $AB=9$. Then $BC^2=BD\cdot AB=45$, $BC=3\sqrt5$, and the area is $\frac12\cdot6\cdot3\sqrt5=9\sqrt5$.

**Answer: $9\sqrt5$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-14.title: Use the altitude
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-14.body:
With $AD=4$, $AB=9$ as above, $CD^2=AD\cdot DB=20$, so $CD=2\sqrt5$ and the area is $\frac12\cdot9\cdot2\sqrt5=9\sqrt5$.

**Answer: $9\sqrt5$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-15.title: Common difference
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-15.body:
The common difference is $d=x-a$, and $4x=a+3d=3x-2a$, so $x=-2a$. Then $b=a+2d=2x-a=-5a$ and $\frac ab=-\frac15$ (with $a\ne0$).

**Answer: $-\frac15$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-17.title: Distance on the number line
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-17.body:
$|x-3|+|x-5|$ is the sum of the distances from $x$ to $3$ and to $5$. Since $3$ and $5$ are $2$ apart, the sum is at least $2$, with equality exactly when $x$ lies between them.

**Answer: $3\le x\le5$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-17.title: Cases
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-17.body:
- $x<3$: $(3-x)+(5-x)=8-2x=2$ gives $x=3$, not in the case.
- $3\le x\le5$: $(x-3)+(5-x)=2$, always true.
- $x>5$: $2x-8=2$ gives $x=5$, not in the case.

**Answer: $3\le x\le5$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-18.title: Cosine addition formula
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-18.body:
The left side is $\cos(2x+3x)=\cos5x$. So $\cos5x=0$: $5x=90^\circ+180^\circ k$, $x=18^\circ+36^\circ k$. With $0\le 5x\le900^\circ$, $5x\in\{90^\circ, 270^\circ, 450^\circ, 630^\circ, 810^\circ\}$, giving $x=18^\circ, 54^\circ, 90^\circ, 126^\circ, 162^\circ$.

**Answer: $18^\circ, 54^\circ, 90^\circ, 126^\circ, 162^\circ$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-19.title: Undo the exponent
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-19.body:
$x^{-2/3}=\frac{16}9$ means $\left(\sqrt[3]x\right)^{2}=\frac9{16}$, so $\sqrt[3]x=\pm\frac34$ and $x=\pm\frac{27}{64}$. The official answer is the positive value, $\frac{27}{64}$; with the real cube root, $x=-\frac{27}{64}$ also works, since $\left(-\frac34\right)^{-2}=\frac{16}9$.

**Answer: $\frac{27}{64}$ (and also $-\frac{27}{64}$)**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-20.title: Perfect squares
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-20.body:
Divisors of $n$ pair up as $d$ and $\frac nd$; they fail to pair only when $d=\frac nd$, so $n$ has an odd number of divisors exactly when it is a perfect square. The three-digit squares are $10^2,\dots,31^2$: $22$ numbers.

**Answer: 22**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-21.title: Add all four sums
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-21.body:
Each number appears in three of the four sums, so $3(a+b+c+d)=100+94+89+80=363$ and $a+b+c+d=121$. Each number is $121$ minus the sum that leaves it out: $121-100=21$, $121-94=27$, $121-89=32$, $121-80=41$.

**Answer: $21, 27, 32, 41$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-22.title: Find the triangle
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-22.body:
With $a\le b\le c$, $a+b+c=8$ and $a+b>c$, we need $c<4$, and $c\ge\frac83$, so $c=3$ and $a+b=5$ with $b\le3$: $(2,3,3)$. The altitude to the side $2$ is $\sqrt{9-1}=2\sqrt2$, so the area is $\frac12\cdot2\cdot2\sqrt2=2\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt2$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-23.title: Period 6
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-23.body:
$\frac1{13}=0.\overline{076923}$, with period $6$. Since $1999=6\cdot333+1$, the $1999$th digit equals the $1$st digit, $0$.

**Answer: 0**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-24.title: Count outcomes with sum 6
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-24.body:
The ordered outcomes with sum $6$ are the solutions of $a+b+c=6$ with each at least $1$: $\binom52=10$ (permutations of $(1,1,4)$: $3$; of $(1,2,3)$: $6$; and $(2,2,2)$: $1$). Only one is $(2,2,2)$, so the probability is $\frac1{10}$.

**Answer: $\frac1{10}$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-26.title: Angle in a semicircle
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-26.body:
$D$ is on the circle with diameter $AB$, so $\angle ADB=90^\circ$: $AD$ is the altitude from $A$ in the equilateral triangle of side $8$. Its length is $\frac{\sqrt3}2\cdot8=4\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $4\sqrt3$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-26.title: Midpoint
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-26.body:
$OD=OB=4$ and $\angle OBD=60^\circ$, so triangle $OBD$ is equilateral and $BD=4$: $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$. Then $AD=\sqrt{8^2-4^2}=4\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $4\sqrt3$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-27.title: Equation of the line
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-27.body:
The slope is $\frac{9-1}{3-(-1)}=2$, so $y-1=2(x+1)$, i.e. $y=2x+3$. Setting $y=0$: $x=-\frac32$.

**Answer: $-\frac32$**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-29.title: Exterior angles
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-29.body:
Each exterior angle is $180^\circ-162^\circ=18^\circ$, and the exterior angles add to $360^\circ$, so there are $\frac{360}{18}=20$ sides.

**Answer: 20**

nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-30.title: Choose above and below
nyciml-1998-99-spring-seniorb-30.body:
The middle number is $5$ when the set contains $5$, two numbers from $\{1,2,3,4\}$ and two from $\{6,\dots,10\}$: $\binom42\binom52=60$ sets. There are $\binom{10}5=252$ sets in all, so the probability is $\frac{60}{252}=\frac5{21}$.

**Answer: $\frac5{21}$**
